title: Three still waiting
stem:
You are an F2 doctor on the acute medical unit. At the 17:00 handover, three of your patients are still waiting for senior review. One of them has a rising early warning score.

The night team is one doctor short, and the night registrar looks worried about the workload.
instruction: Rank in order the following actions in response to this situation (1 = Most appropriate; 5 = Least appropriate).

options.text: Leave the patients on the list, as the night team will see them.
options.detailed: Without a clear handover, the deteriorating patient may not be prioritised. It ranks fourth.

options.text: Tell the patients they will now be seen in the morning.
options.brief: May delay care that one patient needs tonight.
options.detailed: This makes a decision that isn't yours and could mean a deteriorating patient waits. It is the least appropriate option.

options.text: Offer to stay for a short while to help with the sickest patient.
options.brief: A generous, occasional option, but not a solution.
options.detailed: Staying briefly may help on a difficult night, and some doctors would choose to. It ranks third because it isn't sustainable and isn't required.

options.text: Document each patient's outstanding issue clearly in the notes.
options.brief: Supports the night team when they see each patient.
options.detailed: Clear notes help whoever reviews them, especially on a busy night. It ranks second because the verbal handover of the sickest patient matters more.

options.text: Tell the registrar which patients need review, sickest first.
options.brief: A clear, prioritised handover helps the night team focus.
options.detailed: The registrar needs to know who is waiting, and that one patient is deteriorating. Prioritising for them makes the best use of a stretched team. It ranks first.

explanation.issue: This tests how you hand over outstanding work safely when the next team is under pressure.
explanation.keyDetails: Three patients await review. One is deteriorating. The night team is short.
explanation.reasoning: [E] gives a prioritised handover, [D] supports it with documentation, and [C] offers help. [A] lacks prioritisation, and [B] could delay urgent care.
explanation.competing: Some would put staying to help higher. The key prefers a clear handover and documentation, which help all night, whereas staying is a short-term measure.

references.title: National Early Warning Score (NEWS) 2
references.note: Escalating patients with a rising early warning score.
